prompt: The published negativeCapexUnnamed case refuses with PortfolioInputError: "Project "1" has a negative capex (-0.5); capex must be 0 or more". The project carries no name. Which project in the list is it?
options: The first project, because the engine numbers the rows of the inventory from 1, the way a reader counts the rows of the Suite table.
Whichever project carries an id of 1, because the message falls back to the id field when the name field is missing.
The second project, because an unnamed project is named by its position in the list counted from 0.
No project in particular, since "1" counts the refusals raised so far and this case holds a single negative capex.
explanation: The unnamed refusal counts from 0, so "1" is the second entry, and its size does not matter: -0.5 is refused as firmly as -150.

prompt: When negativeCapexRefused fires on project "B" with a capex of -150, what does the optimizer return?
options: No set, no frontier and no risk summary: the PortfolioInputError and its message are the whole result.
The best set among the other projects, with B left out of the inventory and the message attached to the result as a warning.
The best set with B read as a capex of 0, the treatment a negative fail_cost receives without any warning.
The best set with overLimit true, since funding B would add 150 to the limit and the flag marks a limit that stopped meaning a limit.
explanation: A refusal stops the engine and a flag returns an answer; a negative capex is refused, a pos of 1.4 is refused too, and only a negative fail_cost is read as 0 with no warning.

prompt: A user gets past the negative capex refusal by typing 0 in place of -150. Why is that not a safe repair?
options: A capex of 0 gives the project a risked EMV of 0, since the risked EMV is scaled by capex, and a project with EMV of 0 or less is never funded.
The engine refuses a capex of exactly 0 as well, because the message is read as capex must be more than 0, so the edit trades one refusal for another.
The optimizer ranks projects by EMV per million USD before it fills the limit, so a capex of 0 raises a division by zero inside the ranking.
A free project is funded at no cost whenever its EMV is positive, and whatever the negative number carried, such as a receipt, belonged in the NPV and has vanished.
explanation: In freeProjectTightLimit a free project with EMV 10.0000 beside A at capex 100.0000 under a limit of 100.0000 is funded: the engine funds free + A for 70.0000, solveMethod exact.

prompt: Three copies of a project with npv_p50 80 and fail_cost 30 leave pos out, type it as "n/a", and type it as an empty string. What risked EMVs come back?
options: 80.0000 three times, because every pos the engine cannot read as a number falls back to the documented default of 1.
80.0000 for the pos left out, and a PortfolioInputError for the other two, each ending "pos must be a number from 0 to 1".
80.0000, 80.0000 and -30.0000: a non-numeric pos defaults to 1, while an empty string is the number 0 and reads as certain failure.
-30.0000 three times, because a pos that is missing or unreadable is treated as a chance of success of 0 until one is typed in.
explanation: A missing or null pos is the documented default of 1; a pos that is present must be a number from 0 to 1, and a blank or non-numeric one is refused by project name ("has a blank pos", "has a pos that is not a number ("n/a")").

prompt: Project T is entered with capex "abc" beside project U at capex 40, under a limit of 100. What does the optimizer return?
options: T + U at a total capex of 40.0000, because "abc" counts as capex 0 and is neither refused nor flagged.
A PortfolioInputError naming T, "has a capex that is not a finite number ("abc"); capex must be 0 or more", and nothing funded.
U alone at 40.0000, because a capex the engine cannot read as a number drops that project from the inventory before the solve.
T + U with a flag on T, the way a negative working interest returns valid false beside the allocation.
explanation: Every project is checked in list order, capex before pos, before anything is computed; the whole call is refused, so U is not funded either.

prompt: An AFE line described as "Completion" is entered at -0.5 percent progress. What does the engine return?
options: The metrics with that line clamped to 0 percent, since a fraction of a percent below zero is read as a line that has not yet begun.
The metrics with valid false and the message printed as a note, the way the joint venture split reports a negative working interest.
The metrics with that line left out of earned value and out of the budget, so CPI and SPI are computed on the remaining lines.
An AfeInputError, "Cost item "Completion" has negative progress (-0.5 percent). Progress runs from 0 to 100 percent.", and no metrics at all.
explanation: The size does not matter, -0.5 is refused as firmly as -20; clamping to 0 would hide a typing error as a line not yet begun.

prompt: The negative progress message says progress runs from 0 to 100 percent. A published case enters progress of 150 percent. What does the engine do with it?
options: It refuses it with an AfeInputError naming the line: "has progress above 100 percent (150 percent). Progress runs from 0 to 100 percent."
It accepts it and earns beyond the budget, since the message states a range the check enforces only at the lower bound.
It clamps the line to 100 percent, so earned value stops at the budget and the CPI cannot pass the budget over the actuals.
It returns the metrics with a flag on the line, the way the partner split returns its allocation beside valid false.
explanation: Both bounds are enforced. Exactly 100 is accepted and earns the whole budget: the published case reads earned value 140.0000 against actuals of 100.0000, a CPI of 1.400000.

prompt: An AFE with no dates is asked for its metrics as of 30 February and refuses with "asOf is not a valid date". What would a valid as-of date have moved on that AFE?
options: Planned value and SPI, because the engine builds a window that ends on the as-of date whenever the AFE carries no dates of its own.
Earned value and CPI, because each line's progress is prorated to the as-of date before it is multiplied by the line's budget.
Nothing, because with no dates time progress falls back to 1.000000, so the date is refused as an input whatever the arithmetic does with it.
The EAC, because the forecast rule switches every line from its entered forecast to the formula once the as-of date passes the last day of the AFE window.
explanation: A lenient parser would roll 30 February into March and report on a day nobody chose; the published no-dates case returns time progress 1.000000 and SPI 0.250000.

prompt: The published gridOvershoot case offers A (capex 4000.0000), B (2002.0000) and C (1995.0000) under a limit of 6000.0000. What do overLimit and overLimitBy read on the result, and why?
options: true and 2.0000, because A + B fills the limit to within one cell and the flag records the overshoot the engine accepted.
true and 5.0000, because the flag reports any difference between the funded capex and the limit in either direction.
Neither is reported on an exact solve.
false and 0.0000: the exact solve funds A + C at 5995.0000, and a funded set never exceeds the limit.
explanation: overLimit and overLimitBy stay in every optimizer result and read false and 0.0000 on every exact solve; the fallback rounds weights up, so it cannot overshoot either.

prompt: Called with exactStateLimit 2, the published gridOvershootFallback case runs A (capex 4000.0000), B (2002.0000) and C (1995.0000) against 6000.0000 on a grid of 2000 cells at resolution 3.000000. Why does it fund A + C and leave A + B out?
options: Every weight is rounded up, A to 1334 cells, B to 668 and C to 665, so A + B needs 2002 cells and A + C needs 1999.
The limit and every capex are whole numbers, so the fallback runs at 1 million USD per cell and A + B is 2.0000 over it.
The fallback admits any set within one cell of the limit, and A + C is kept because it leaves 5.0000 unspent.
B and C round to the same number of cells, so the grid cannot tell them apart and keeps whichever of the two was entered last.
explanation: Rounding up means any set that fits the grid fits the limit in money. The result reads solveMethod grid-feasible, overLimit false and optimalityGap 20.0000, the bound from the same grid with every weight rounded down.

prompt: The published gridUndershoot case offers W, X and Y at capex 1499.0000 and Z at 1502.0000, with EMVs 200.0000, 210.0000, 220.0000 and 230.0000, under a limit of 6000.0000. What does the optimizer fund?
options: X + Y + Z at 4500.0000 for 660.0000, since rounding makes the four together weigh more cells than the grid holds.
Y + Z at 3001.0000 for 450.0000, since the optimizer funds the highest EMV per million USD first and stops at half the limit.
All four at capex 5999.0000 for 860.0000, solved exactly with optimalityGap 0.0000 and 1.0000 left unspent.
W + X + Y + Z with overLimit true, since 5999.0000 is within one cell of the limit and the flag marks a set that fills it.
explanation: The solve is exact on the capex as typed. Only a stated small exactStateLimit forces the fallback grid, where the published gridUndershootFallback funds X + Y + Z at 660.0000 with optimalityGap 200.0000.

prompt: A joint venture split on a cost of 1000.00 enters partner interests of 30 and -20. Is that a refusal or a flag, and what comes back?
options: A refusal: an AfeInputError naming partner "B" and no allocation at all, the same treatment the AFE engine gives a cost line entered with negative progress or a bad as-of date.
A flag: valid false with the engine note naming partner "B" and its -20.00 percent, and the allocation still shown with the operator at 90.0000 percent.
A flag, with the -20 interest clamped to 0, so partner "B" is billed nothing and the operator is shown carrying 70.0000 percent.
Neither: the split nets the two interests to 10 percent, so the operator carries 90.0000 percent and valid stays true.
explanation: Partner amounts read 300.00 and -200.00 and the operator 900.00; the AFE summary prints the note beside the allocation.

prompt: The published empty AFE has no lines, no budget and no spend. Why does it report SPI null?
options: The empty AFE has no dates, so time progress falls back to 1 and its whole budget of zero is planned, which prints SPI 0.000000.
SPI copies CPI, which is null because nothing has been spent.
The null rule applies only up to the start day, and an AFE with no lines is treated as one that has not yet started.
An AFE with no budget has no plan to measure schedule against, so SPI is null with spiStatus "no-budget".
explanation: CPI is null too, with cpiStatus "no-spend"; the Suite's SPI tile reads "N/A" with "No budget to measure schedule against".

prompt: OFON-1's S-curve is drawn by viewers in UTC, Lagos, Tokyo and America/Los_Angeles. What does each see as the first point?
options: Feb 27 with Planned 0 in every zone, because the window, the as-of date, the monthly step and the labels are all read in UTC.
Jan 27 west of UTC, because the window is parsed as UTC midnight while the months are stepped and labelled in local time.
Feb 27 in UTC and a point dated the viewer's local start day elsewhere, because each zone draws its own calendar.
A curve opening a month before the window in zones west of UTC, to show commitments placed before the start.
explanation: The published case with a February start labels Feb in every zone; the same AFE draws the same curve wherever it is read.

prompt: In the Suite the correlation slider stops at 0.9, where OKONO's 600.0000 set reads stdDev 232.0795 and P(loss) 0.049500. How should that top value be read?
options: As the engine's clamp: any correlation above 0.9 is cut back to 0.9, which is what the published clampAbove case exists to show.
As the largest correlation the simulation can hold, because a correlation of 1 makes sqrt(1 - rho) zero and the draws collapse.
As the app's limit alone: the engine accepts 1 and reads stdDev 239.8888 and P(loss) 0.059000, which the screen cannot set.
As a harmless cap, because the emv of 402.7500 does not move with correlation, so the last step of the slider would change nothing that is reported.
explanation: The published clampAbove case reads correlation used 1.000000; the slider stopping at 0.9 is a property of the app as it stands, so the most correlated case has to be run on the engine and named.
